title: Connect Request shown when privacy is disabled
body:
**Description**
V5.0.1 introduces a bug where connect request dialog is displayed even with privacy mode turned off. This issue was not present in v5.0.0

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to settings and disable privacy.
2. Refresh the page.
3. Notice Connect Request dialog

**Expected behavior**
The Connect Request dialog should not be displayed when privacy is turned off.

**Browser details**
 - OS: Windows 10 Pro
 - Browser Chrome version 70.0.3538.77 (Official Build) (64-bit)
 - MetaMask Version 5.0.1
 - Beta UI
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Hi @DaneWiid1, thanks for taking the time to file this issue. We recently simplified our implementation of the "privacy mode" settings option. Specifically, turning this option "off" makes it so your accounts are always exposed to the dapps you visit, but this doesn't prevent the approval popup from showing if a dapp explicitly calls `ethereum.enable()`. The "privacy mode" settings option was only ever meant to allow users to continue to use legacy dapps that may be slow to update to the new API. However, if a dapp is already calling the new API, meaning their code is already updated to handle the approval popup, users will still see the approval popup regardless of whether "privacy mode" is "on" or "off". It should also be noted that this settings option is temporary: it will eventually be defaulted to "on" and ultimately removed altogether in future releases, making private browsing the only option for users.

Thanks again for reaching out. Let us know if you have any additional questions while testing.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
Thanks for the explanation @bitpshr. I think it's easy to misunderstand the behavior of "Privacy mode" given the name. We also expected connect requests to not show as long as this was off.

Perhaps something like "Legacy Support" with the on/off meanings switched (Privacy mode "off" == Legacy support "on") would've reduced confusion a bit. I guess either way it'll all be removed soon, so it's no big deal.

comments.author: Participant 4
Participant 5
comments.body:
If enabling or disabling Privacy Mode has no effect, why include it in the interface at all? The user has no meaningful choice, so the option should just be removed OR the behavior of the option should be made consistent with all the documentation that clearly says what the behavior should be.

I agree with the original rationale behind adding this option and progressing toward making it on by default.  This gives dapp developers a chance to make the necessary changes and test them out.  However, if the option is going to be in the interface, it should give users a meaningful choice where the meaning matches all the documentation of what the meaning is supposed to be, in many places, that are not updated and show no sign that they are going to be.  I believe it would be significantly better to restore the original, well-documented behavior of the Privacy Mode setting.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
@wbt,

> If enabling or disabling Privacy Mode has no effect, why include it in the interface at all?

This settings option does have an effect, just not a visual one: accounts are either automatically exposed to dapps if this option is disabled, or not automatically exposed if this option is enabled.

Also, as stated earlier, this settings option is purely temporary so legacy dapps can work for the time being, and was never meant to reduce user-facing prompts on dapps that already call the new API. Our privacy mode [blog post](https://medium.com/metamask/introducing-privacy-mode-42549d4870fa) also states that users may still see the prompt with the option disabled as dapps update proactively:

> At first, Privacy Mode will be opt-in (and turned “off” by default). Even if you haven’t turned Privacy Mode “on” yet, we want to make it clear what’s happening under the hood, so you may start seeing the “Connect to this site” dialog as you use your favorite dapps.

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body:
> This settings option does have an effect, just not a visual one: **accounts are** either **automatically exposed to dapps if this option is disabled**, or not automatically exposed if this option is enabled.

That's what I expected, too, based on all the documentation and logical software behavior.  That's apparently not how the software actually behaves.  If the option is disabled, accounts are apparently **not** automatically exposed to dapps, and if the user clicks "cancel" on the popup the dapp apparently does not ever get the account exposed unless the user later returns and clicks "connect."  

This disconnect between our and even your expert expectations of how the software *should* behave and how it actually *does* behave is the basis and trigger for my bug report (#5971) and apparently this one as well.

comments.author: Participant 6
comments.body: So apps that *are* implementing the new API are stuck with a crummy UX, where the popup appears even though the user has explicitely requested not to see it, and the app has no way (that I can find) of preventing the popup from being shown, nor any way of anticipating that the popup is going to be shown.  It is an unavoidable, meaningless popup that is presented to the user for no explainable reason, and the app has no means of ameliorating the situation.
